cbt.title: CBT toolkit
cbt.intro: Simple, evidence-based exercises from cognitive behavioural therapy. These are self-help tools for learning, not treatment or a diagnosis.

thought.title: Thought record
thought.intro: Slow a distressing thought down and look at it from more angles. Records are encrypted in your browser with your vault passphrase.
thought.situationHint: Where were you, who was there, what happened?
thought.balancedHint: A fairer way to say it, using both sides of the evidence.
thought.intensityAfter: How strong is the feeling now (0 to 100)?
thought.required: Please fill in the situation, the automatic thought and a balanced thought.
thought.saveError: We could not save this record. Please try again.
thought.loadError: We could not load your thought records.
thought.crisisTitle: It sounds like things are very heavy right now
thought.crisisBody: Your record stays encrypted on your side. Please reach out to one of these free, confidential helplines, available 24/7:

activity.title: Behavioural activation planner
activity.intro: When mood is low, small planned activities can lift it. Plan something, do it, then rate your mood. Stored on this device only.
activity.name: Activity
activity.empty: Nothing planned yet. Start with something small.
activity.required: Please name the activity and pick a time.

worry.title: Worry-time scheduler
worry.intro: Pick a daily 15 to 20 minute slot for worrying. When a worry shows up at other times, park it here and come back to it later. Stored on this device only.
worry.parkPlaceholder: Write the worry in one line
worry.reviewHint: At worry time, ask of each one: can I do something about it? If yes, plan one step. If no, practise letting it go.

breathing.title: 4-7-8 breathing tool
breathing.guideInhale: Breathe in slowly and deeply through your nose...
breathing.guideHold: Hold your breath gently and relax your shoulders...
breathing.guideExhale: Exhale completely and steadily through your mouth...
breathing.complete: Well done. You finished all the cycles.
breathing.reducedMotion: Reduced motion is on, so the circle stays still. Follow the words and numbers.
breathing.medical: If breath-holding makes you dizzy, breathe normally and stop. This is a relaxation exercise, not medical advice.

grounding.title: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding method
grounding.intro: When panic or racing thoughts take over, anchoring your five senses can bring you back to the present moment.

s5.title: Acknowledge 5 things you can SEE around you
items: A shadow or beam of light

s4.title: Acknowledge 4 things you can physically TOUCH

s3.title: Acknowledge 3 things you can HEAR right now

s1.title: Acknowledge 1 thing you can TASTE
items: A sip of cold water or mint

carePlan.title: Your care plan ideas
carePlan.disclaimer: These are general wellbeing ideas for students, not a diagnosis or treatment plan.
carePlan.step1: Practise 4-7-8 breathing or take a mindful 10-minute walk between classes.
carePlan.step2: Aim for 7 or more hours of sleep. Switch off bright study screens 30 minutes before bed.
carePlan.step3: Book a private, judgement-free session with a campus counsellor.

rain.title: Monsoon rain
rain.freq: Soft noise with a low-pass filter
rain.desc: Gentle rainfall and distant thunder to soften exam overthinking.

bowl.title: 432 Hz singing bowl
bowl.freq: 432 Hz tone with a slow acoustic beat
bowl.desc: A warm, steady bowl tone many people find calming.

solfeggio.title: 528 Hz tone
solfeggio.freq: 528 Hz with a 264 Hz grounding octave
solfeggio.desc: A calm, steady tone for winding down. It is a relaxation aid, not a treatment.

delta.title: Delta sleep beat
delta.desc: A slow, low beat to help you drift off at night.
